text: What was Octavian's birth name before Caesar's adoption took effect?
Before becoming Caesar's heir, Octavian was related to Julius Caesar in what way by blood?
Which parent connected Octavian to the Julian family line of Caesar?
Where was Octavian studying and training when news of Caesar's assassination reached him in 44 BCE?
What document made Octavian Caesar's posthumously adopted son and principal heir?
After accepting Caesar's inheritance, what name did Octavian technically assume?
In modern writing, why is the name Octavian commonly still used after 44 BCE?
choices: It was his formal imperial title
It appears on most of his coins
It helps distinguish him from Julius Caesar

text: Which senior Caesarian initially tried to block Octavian from fully accessing Caesar's inheritance?
What slogan became central to Octavian's early political identity after Caesar's death?
Octavian's claim as Divi Filius depended on Caesar eventually receiving what status?
Whose veterans did Octavian court aggressively in 44 BCE to build an armed following?
Which famous orator briefly treated Octavian as a useful ally against Antony in 44 to 43 BCE?
The speeches Cicero delivered attacking Antony during Octavian's rise are known by what name?
In 43 BCE Octavian was granted imperium by the Senate while still being unusually young for which kind of career stage?
Which city was the center of the 43 BCE campaign against Antony that first brought Octavian into major warfare?
At Mutina, which of the consuls fighting Antony died in the campaign alongside Hirtius?
The deaths of both consuls in 43 BCE most directly benefited Octavian in what way?
choices: He became the uncontested commander of Caesarian troops in the field
He received Egypt as a province

text: When the Senate hesitated after Mutina, Octavian marched on which city to force his election to the consulship?
How old was Octavian when he first became consul in 43 BCE, a striking breach of convention?
Which law formally created the three-man board of Octavian, Antony, and Lepidus?
The Second Triumvirate differed from the earlier alliance of Caesar, Pompey, and Crassus because it was what?
What brutal policy did Octavian share responsibility for soon after the formation of the Second Triumvirate?
Which prominent Roman was among the most famous victims of the triumviral proscriptions?
What did the proscriptions chiefly accomplish for the triumvirs besides terrorizing opponents?
choices: They funded armies and confiscated enemy wealth

text: Which battle in 42 BCE eliminated Brutus and Cassius as the leading liberator commanders?
At Philippi, which triumvir was generally regarded as the more capable battlefield commander than Octavian?
Ancient accounts often portray Octavian's personal performance at Philippi in what unflattering way?
After Philippi, Octavian's main sphere of responsibility within the triumviral order was broadly which region?
What immediate domestic problem most burdened Octavian in Italy after Philippi?
Which conflict arose from tensions over Italian land confiscations and involved Fulvia and Lucius Antonius?
The Perusine War takes its name from which besieged Italian city?
Who was Fulvia in relation to Mark Antony during the Perusine crisis?
Lucius Antonius, Octavian's opponent in the Perusine War, was Antony's what?
What was the political effect of Octavian's victory in the Perusine War?
choices: It drove Antony permanently out of Roman politics
It strengthened Octavian's grip on Italy before reconciliation
It handed Sicily to Sextus Pompey
It made Lepidus master of Rome

text: Which pact in 40 BCE temporarily reconciled Octavian and Antony after their recent tensions?
The reconciliation at Brundisium was reinforced by Antony's marriage to which woman?
Octavia, used in the reconciliation with Antony, was Octavian's what?
Which rival son of Pompey the Great remained a major threat to Octavian by controlling key sea lanes?
Sextus Pompey's power base was centered above all on which island?
Why was Sextus Pompey especially dangerous to Octavian's regime in Italy?
choices: He controlled the grain supply routes
He held the treasury on the Capitol

text: Which agreement in 39 BCE briefly settled relations between the triumvirs and Sextus Pompey?
Octavian's early attempts against Sextus Pompey exposed a weakness in what branch of warfare?
Which lieutenant became indispensable to Octavian by rebuilding his naval position against Sextus Pompey?
What specialized harbor complex did Agrippa construct to train and launch Octavian's fleet before the Sicilian war?
Which battle in 36 BCE decisively broke Sextus Pompey's power?
After Sextus Pompey's defeat, which triumvir tried unsuccessfully to claim Sicily and was then politically reduced by Octavian?
How did Octavian neutralize Lepidus after the Sicilian campaign?
choices: He stripped him of power while sparing his life and priesthood
He forced him to marry Julia

text: Which major religious office was Lepidus allowed to retain even after losing real political power?
By the later 30s BCE, the collapse of Lepidus left Octavian and Antony in what basic strategic relationship?
choices: The two dominant rivals in the Roman world

text: Which western political advisor is most associated with managing Octavian's civilian strategy and elite relations rather than battlefield command?
In Octavian's propaganda war against Antony, Cleopatra was used above all to depict Antony as what?
choices: Subservient to an alien eastern monarchy

text: Which ceremony of 34 BCE gave Octavian valuable material to portray Antony as abandoning Roman norms?
Whose supposed will did Octavian dramatically publicize to inflame Roman opinion against Antony?
What claim in Antony's will was especially useful to Octavian's campaign against him?
choices: That Antony wanted to restore the Republic
That Antony wished burial in Alexandria
That Antony planned to adopt Octavian

text: Rome did not formally declare war on Antony at first, but instead on whom?
This formal declaration helped Octavian frame the coming conflict as what?
choices: A foreign war against eastern corruption rather than another Roman civil war

text: Which admiral commanded Octavian's fleet with decisive effectiveness in the campaign of 31 BCE?
What was the decisive battle of 31 BCE that shattered Antony and Cleopatra's position?
Actium was fought primarily as what kind of engagement?
Where was Actium fought geographically?
choices: Off western Greece near the Ambracian Gulf

text: One major advantage Octavian's side held before Actium came from Agrippa's earlier seizure of what?
choices: Key coastal positions that strained Antony's supply lines

text: Which feature of Antony's camp before Actium weakened him over time even without a pitched land battle?
choices: Loss of all cavalry in Spain

text: After Cleopatra's squadron broke through at Actium, Antony did what according to the traditional account?
What city fell to Octavian in 30 BCE, effectively ending the final round of Roman civil wars?
Which two leading rivals died in the aftermath of Octavian's victory in Egypt?
Why was Caesarion especially threatening to Octavian's position after the conquest of Egypt?
choices: He claimed to be Julius Caesar's natural son

text: What happened to Caesarion after Octavian secured Egypt?
Egypt under Octavian was unusual among Roman possessions because it was governed in what especially controlled way?
choices: As the personal domain of the princeps through an equestrian prefect
By the Senate as a peaceful province

text: Why were senators restricted from entering Egypt without permission under the new order?
choices: The Nile floods were considered sacred
Octavian wanted to prevent rivals from gaining a wealthy strategic base

text: After Actium and Alexandria, Octavian could present himself as the bringer of what after long civil conflict?
Which temple vowed earlier by Octavian and associated with vengeance for Caesar became central to his political symbolism?
Octavian's public image after the civil wars depended heavily on claiming he had done what to the Republic in appearance?
Which year marks the settlement in which Octavian theatrically handed powers back and then received a new political arrangement from the Senate?
What honorific name did the Senate grant Octavian in 27 BCE?
Before 27 BCE, modern historians usually prefer what name to distinguish him from the later emperor Augustus?
The title Augustus was useful because it suggested elevated prestige without overtly claiming which politically dangerous title?
What title emphasizing preeminence among citizens, rather than monarchy, fit the political style Octavian cultivated?
The settlement of 27 BCE left Octavian in control of provinces containing most of what crucial resource?
Why was holding the main military provinces more important than possessing a long list of old republican offices?
choices: It guaranteed command over the army
It removed the need for law courts
It made him sole censor automatically

text: Which concept best describes the extra-legal prestige Octavian translated into durable political supremacy?
In 23 BCE Octavian adjusted his position after a political scare by giving up the regular consulship and relying more on what enduring package?
That change in 23 BCE matters for Octavian as a historical figure because it completed the transition from victorious warlord into what?
choices: A stable princeps with lasting constitutional cover

text: What military title, acclaimed repeatedly by troops, remained an important part of Octavian's public persona even before Augustus became his main name?
Which close associate was more central to Octavian's naval and military victories than to literary patronage?
Which associate was more central to Octavian's political management at Rome and cultural circle than to fleet command?
What made Octavian's rise especially remarkable in Roman constitutional terms?
choices: He never used armies at all
He advanced from youth to supreme power through repeated exceptions to normal office-holding rules
He inherited the throne from his father
He ruled first as king of Egypt

text: Which phrase best captures the political balancing act Octavian mastered after victory over Antony?
choices: Power without the name of kingship

text: Octavian's repeated emphasis on avenging Caesar linked his cause not just to inheritance but to what moral posture?
choices: Submission to the Senate as master

text: Which battle let Octavian claim he had completed vengeance against the liberators before he later turned on Antony?
Which conflict let Octavian shift from avenger of Caesar to defender of Rome against an easternized rival?
Why did Octavian's propagandists find Antony's association with Cleopatra more useful than his mere rivalry with Octavian?
choices: It let them recast a civil war as resistance to foreign domination
It proved Antony had killed Caesar
It showed Antony lacked any army
It allowed Octavian to ally with Brutus

text: What does the arc from Apollonia in 44 BCE to Augustus in 27 BCE most clearly show about Octavian?
choices: He was only a passive heir
He turned inheritance, military opportunism, and political theater into sole rule

text: Which event most directly ended the practical independence of Ptolemaic Egypt?
Which of these figures was not one of the three legally empowered triumvirs alongside Octavian?
During the years before 27 BCE, Octavian's strongest formal claim to exceptional status combined Caesar's legacy with repeated military acclamation under which label?
choices: Imperator Caesar, son of the deified one

text: Which problem did Octavian solve more successfully than any rival of his generation: how to do what after civil war?
choices: Keep one-man supremacy while disguising it within Roman norms

text: What sequence best matches the broad order of Octavian's major struggles?
choices: Mutina, Philippi, Perusia, Sicily against Sextus, Actium

text: Which opponent was primarily a maritime threat rather than a senatorial assassin or triumviral colleague?
Which opponent was primarily a colleague turned eastern rival rather than an immediate enemy after Caesar's death?
What was Octavian's most important political asset in 44 BCE before he had proven military skill of his own?
choices: Direct command of the eastern legions

text: What was Agrippa's victory at Naulochus to Octavian's rise?
choices: A minor skirmish with no consequence
The elimination of the Sicilian blockade threat that had destabilized Italy

text: What was Actium to Octavian's rise?
choices: The decisive defeat of his final great Roman rival

text: What was the grant of the name Augustus to Octavian?
choices: A public acknowledgment of his new, elevated but non-royal supremacy
